about: Estate and marriage (run Finish everything partly built, Part 11): the rules the estate basics, the inheritance simulator and Married or partners? stand on. Each line names its source, the page and the day it was checked. The numbers themselves are in data/reference-2026.json (estate), with the same sources on the assumptions list.
how: Checked on 2026-11-26 by a web search limited to each agency's own site (irs.gov, federalregister.gov, ssa.gov, tax.ny.gov, nyc.gov, finra.org, nycourts.gov); the pages could not be opened directly from the build machine. Rules change: check the page on the day you use it.
lawyer: This is not legal or tax advice. It is a summary to bring to a lawyer, who turns it into the real papers and checks it against the law on the day you sign.

beneficiaryWins.text: The beneficiary form on a retirement account, and a transfer-on-death form on a brokerage account, usually beat what a will says. Check who is named on each account.
beneficiaryWins.source: FINRA, Retirement Accounts; Plan Now to Smooth the Transfer of Your Brokerage Account Assets on Death

noWillNy.text: With no will, New York law gives what you leave to a spouse and children, then parents, then brothers and sisters. A partner you are not married to, and friends, get nothing by default.
noWillNy.source: New York courts, CourtHelp: Intestacy, When There Is No Will

stepUp.text: For something inherited (shares, a home), the starting point for tax is usually its value on the date of death, not what the person paid. The gain while they owned it is never taxed as income.

inheritIncome.text: An inheritance is not income for federal income tax. What comes out of an inherited traditional IRA or 401(k) is, in the year it comes out.
inheritIncome.source: IRS, Gifts and inheritances FAQ; Publication 590-B (2025)

lifeInsurance.text: Life insurance paid to you because the insured person died is generally not income, and you do not report it. Interest on it is.
lifeInsurance.source: IRS, Life Insurance and Disability Insurance Proceeds FAQ

tenYear.text: Most people who inherit a traditional IRA or 401(k) must empty it by December 31 of the 10th year after the year of death. A death in 2026: by December 31 2036.

tenYearYearly.text: If the owner had already started their required withdrawals, the heir also takes a withdrawal every year in years 1 to 9, and empties it in year 10. The final regulations (July 19 2024) apply from 2025; for 2021 to 2024 the IRS did not count the missed yearly ones (Notices 2022-53 and 2024-35). The yearly minimum comes from the IRS life expectancy table: the account firm works it out.
tenYearYearly.source: Federal Register, Required Minimum Distributions, final regulations, July 19 2024 (TD 10001); IRS Notice 2024-35

eligible.text: Five kinds of heir have more choices than the 10 years: a surviving spouse, the owner's child under 21, a disabled or chronically ill person, and anyone not more than 10 years younger than the owner. A spouse can also treat the IRA as their own. A child's 10 years start at 21.
eligible.source: IRS, Retirement topics: Beneficiary; Publication 590-B (2025); final regulations July 19 2024 (age 21)

federalExclusion.text: Federal estate tax starts only above $15,000,000 for a death in 2026 (the basic exclusion amount, set by Public Law 119-21 of July 4 2025). Most estates owe none.
federalExclusion.source: IRS, What's new: Estate and gift tax; 2026 Instructions for Form 709

marital.text: What passes outright to a surviving spouse who is a US citizen comes off the estate for federal estate tax (the marital deduction). A spouse can also keep the unused part of the exclusion (portability) if the executor files Form 706 for it. None of this is open to partners who are not married.
marital.source: IRS, Frequently asked questions on estate taxes; Publication 559 (2025)

giftAnnual.text: You can give each person up to $19,000 in 2026 with no gift tax form. Between spouses who are US citizens, gifts have no limit.
giftAnnual.source: IRS, What's new: Estate and gift tax

nyExclusion.text: New York estate tax starts above $7,350,000 for a death from January 1 to December 31 2026 (the New York basic exclusion amount). New York has no portability between spouses.
nyExclusion.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance, Estate tax

nyCliff.text: The New York cliff: between $7,350,000 and 105% of it ($7,717,500) the credit shrinks fast, and above 105% it is gone, so the whole estate is taxed, not only the part over the line.
nyCliff.source: NY Department of Taxation and Finance, Instructions for Form ET-706 (line 3 and its worksheet); TSB-M-14(6)M

dpFederal.text: Registered domestic partners are not married for federal tax. They cannot file jointly or as married filing separately; each files single, or head of household if they qualify.
dpFederal.source: IRS, Answers to frequently asked questions for registered domestic partners and individuals in civil unions; Publication 555

dpCover.text: Job health cover is tax-free for you, your spouse, your dependents and your children under 27. Cover for a partner who is none of these counts as taxable pay (imputed income).
dpCover.source: IRS, Publication 15-B (2026), accident and health benefits

dpCoverNy.text: On the New York State employee plan (NYSHIP), cover for a domestic partner who is not a tax dependent is a taxable benefit for federal and New York tax, and for Social Security and Medicare.
dpCoverNy.source: NY Department of Civil Service, PS-425 (4/2026) NYSHIP Domestic Partner Enrollment Application

nycRegister.text: New York City registers domestic partnerships at the City Clerk: both 18 or older, unmarried, living together, both NYC residents (or one a City employee), in person by appointment, $35. There is no statewide registry in New York.
nycRegister.source: NYC Office of the City Clerk, Domestic Partnership Registration

ssSpouse.text: A spouse can get up to half of the other's full benefit, after one year of marriage (sooner as the parent of their child). A divorced spouse needs 10 years of marriage.
ssSpouse.source: Social Security Administration, What are the marriage requirements to receive spouse's benefits? (KA-01999)

ssSurvivor.text: A surviving spouse can get the larger benefit of the one who died, after 9 months of marriage (with exceptions, such as an accident), from 60 (50 with a disability).
ssSurvivor.source: Social Security Administration, Who can get Survivor benefits

ssPartner.text: Social Security counts a domestic partnership or civil union as a marriage only where the state would give the partner a spouse's share with no will. New York gives an unmarried partner no share, so a New York partnership gets no spouse or survivor benefit.
ssPartner.source: Social Security Administration, POMS GN 00210.004 Non-Marital Legal Relationships; New York courts, Intestacy
